newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon marks Israeli invasion anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon marks Israeli invasion anniversary.

text.p: Lebanon briefly ground to a halt on Friday in protest against Israel's 19-year occupation of south Lebanon.

Motorists stopped their cars in Beirut as shops, banks and public institutions observed a five-minute work stoppage called by Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, Lebanon's leading Shi'ite Moslem politician, for the 19th anniversary of Israel's first invasion of the country. The Israelis have not left since.
Similar work stoppages were reported in other cities.

State-run television played the national anthem before showing pictures of carnage from a 17-day Israeli blitz last April against Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon in which some 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed.
Israel first invaded in 1978 and has remained since, in south Lebanon occupying about 11 percent of the country's total area.
"This stoppage is a symbolic act. We are thinking right now of those Lebanese living under the Israeli bombardment," Lina Sbeiti, an employee at Beirut's First National Bank, told Reuters.
"We are expressing our commitment to our people in the south, and showing our respect to those surviving the Israeli occupation," Mohammad Tabsh, also a bank employee, said.

Like thousands of Lebanese, Tabsh wore a yellow ribbon on his chest with the number 425 inscribed on it -- a reference to U.N. Security Council Resolution 425 of 1978 calling for an immediate Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon.

Israeli forces poured into south Lebanon in 1978 after Palestinian fighters staged raids into the Jewish state. In 1982 Israeli forces invaded again, reaching the capital Beirut, driving most PLO fighters from the country and killing some 20,000 people.

In 1985, Israel pulled out most of its forces but kept some 1,000 soldiers and about 3,000 allied Lebanese militiamen holding a 15-km (nine-mile) deep zone in south Lebanon to stop cross-border guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
